title: Social Media Screen-Time Spillover
dataSources: RescueTime activity (`rescuetime:activity`), screen-time exports (`screentime:usage`), GitHub events (`github:personal`), habit-tracker logs (`habit:entry`), calendar exports (`calendar:event`), email metadata (`email:metadata`), password-audit reports (`passwordmanager:audit`).
app: Screen-time / RescueTime exports, GitHub personal activity, habit/journal trackers, password-audit exports, and calendar/email feeds via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=screentime:usage
| where match(app_name,"(?i)instagram|tiktok|twitter|x|facebook|reddit")
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(minutes) as social_minutes by _time
| where social_minutes>60
| sort - social_minutes
description: Adds up the daily minutes spent in social apps and flags the days where idle checking clearly expanded into real time consumption.
value: A lot of digital drift happens five minutes at a time; turning it into a total helps you decide whether the trade-off felt worth it.
implementation: Forward screen-time exports with app names; review the high-social days and compare them to mood, sleep, or focus metrics if desired.
visualization: Daily chart of total social-media minutes.
grandmaExplanation: It maps when quick social-media checks have turned into more than an hour of the day.
